standard_prerequisites.name: Insertion of a short chord
standard_prerequisites.statement: insrt_i(m) is the matching obtained by inserting a short chord joining i and i+1 and shifting the later vertices by two.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the operation applied to both matchings in the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Knuth equivalence generated by elementary transformations
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two matchings are Knuth equivalent when one is obtained from the other by a sequence of elementary Knuth transformations.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is both the hypothesis and the conclusion, and the proof inducts on the length of such a sequence.

standard_prerequisites.name: Independence of the insertion position
standard_prerequisites.statement: Inserting a short chord at any two positions gives Knuth equivalent matchings.
standard_prerequisites.use: It lets the proof restrict to the last position.

core_obligations: Use the independence of the insertion position to reduce the claim to the case i = N+1 (source line 1173).

Write the second matching as the image of the first under a sequence of elementary Knuth transformations and argue by induction on the length of that sequence, the empty case being immediate (source lines 1173-1175).

In the induction step, apply the induction hypothesis to reduce to a single elementary transformation, and show directly that inserting the chord at the last position commutes with that transformation (source line 1175).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to the last insertion position and set up the induction on the number of elementary Knuth transformations.
Reduce to one elementary transformation and check the insertion against it.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 1167-1170: if two matchings of the same size are Knuth equivalent, then inserting a short chord at the same index in both gives Knuth equivalent matchings again. The proof (source lines 1172-1176) needs two reductions that the statement does not show: first the position of the insertion has to be normalised to the last one, which uses the independently proved invariance of the insertion position, and then the number of elementary Knuth transformations joining the two matchings has to be reduced by induction, leaving the case of a single elementary transformation, which is checked against the explicit vertex-shifting formula of the insertion.
